A.title: Motor's own 18 AWG leads, uncut, down the back face
A.conductor: SE 2816 leads as supplied (18 AWG, 25 cm), trimmed to length; no splice
A.changes: hand-base grooves exit at the back edge; lead groove in the top block
A.note: runs hot: 27 W/m per lead at hover

B.title: Copper strip busbars taped to the back face
B.conductor: 3 x K&S 0.5 x 6.35 mm copper strip (3.2 mm2), Kapton-wrapped; motor stubs soldered on
B.changes: as A, plus a 22 mm wide flat on the top block
B.note: lowest loss; most hand work (cut, bend, insulate)

C.title: 14 AWG silicone down the back face, joined to short motor stubs
C.conductor: same 14 AWG as the arm side and the B.6 bullet grooves; motor leads cut to 20 mm
C.note: joints sit on the back face under the cage

D.title: 16 AWG down the back face (lighter C)
D.conductor: 16 AWG silicone, joined to 20 mm motor stubs

E.title: Split: one lead up the front face, two up the back
E.conductor: 14 AWG; front lead between the servo face and the cords
E.changes: as A on both faces; shortest hand-base runs
E.clearance: front lead 0.7 mm from a moving cord
E.note: tight to moving cords; stray field at the servo encoders

F.title: C inside a printed cover rail
F.conductor: 14 AWG in a clip-on PA-CF channel on the back face
F.changes: as C, plus the rail (2 clips on the frame)
F.note: protects the leads in a crash; one more printed part

G.title: Earlier idea: 18 AWG down both side corridors
G.conductor: motor leads, one at the front (y 23.5), two at the back
G.changes: 2 tunnels in the top block + plate notches
G.clearance: front lead -0.5 mm: rubs two moving cords
G.note: rejected: the first search left the cords out

H.title: Move the servos to open a centre channel
H.conductor: 14 AWG up the middle; servo stack split by 10 mm
H.changes: frame, spools, cords and idlers all move
H.note: not needed: the back face is already empty; hand 5 mm wider
